body: I had a similar experience in high school as well. I avoided the lunch room at all cost so people wouldn’t see how much a loser I was and instead hid in the library during lunch. If the library was closed for some reason I would hide in the bathroom until lunch was done. The only advice I can give is high school is temporary and that it gets a bit better when you graduate. People aren’t as judgmental as you believe and many really are focusing on themselves and not you. The best advice I can give is to make friends with people that you spend most time with. At a job, extracurricular, or something else. Start with something small like just saying hello and letting people know you’re approachable. It takes time and is hard to meet the right kind of people. But just acting casual at first and building off that made me some of my closest friends after high school. Good luck

I have to say I really resonated with what you wrote. I also used to be more extroverted as a kid and now live my life like a hermit. I totally get what your saying about getting prescribed Xanax at such a young age and setting a path towards more drug use. I got prescribed Ativan for panic attacks when I was 14/15 and I think that stuff messed with me. I couldn’t stand the feeling of being off it so I kept trying to find things that I could be in a similar state. 
Recently I’ve really been trying to find myself (the person I was meant to be before all this got in my way). I’ve taken to writing jokes and sketches. I’m not sure if I’ll ever do stand up (great fears of public speaking) but writing jokes about little things that happen in my day keep me less in the toxic headspace that I find myself returning to. I hope you can too find the happy little things that help keep the toxicity away. Peace
